report.source_text: We performed whole-body bone scintigraphy with 99mTc hydroxymethylene. The findings showed multiple lesions with an increased uptake in the bilateral ribs, lumbar spine, knee joints, ankle joints, and metatarsal bones, indicating insidious pathological fractures caused by hypophosphatemic osteomalacia.

clinician.final_diagnosis: the 11-year history of ADV treatment was considered to be the main cause of his Fanconi syndrome and hypophosphatemic osteomalacia.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic HBV infection, treated with adefovir dipivoxil (ADV) since 2005, presented with chronic kidney disease, treatment-resistant joint pain, and mild bilateral lower limb pain. Initial laboratory tests revealed findings consistent with Fanconi syndrome, including hyperphosphatasemia, severe hypophosphatemia, hypouricemia, increased fractional excretion of phosphate and uric acid, normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, highly elevated urinary β2-microglobulin, and glycosuria. Whole-body bone scintigraphy indicated insidious pathological fractures caused by hypophosphatemic osteomalacia. Following the diagnosis, ADV treatment was switched to entecavir. Subsequently, the patient's hyperphosphatasemia, hypophosphatemia, and metabolic acidosis gradually improved, and his lower limb pain did not recur, supporting the causal link between long-term ADV use and the Fanconi syndrome with associated hypophosphatemic osteomalacia.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient had chronic HBV infection and was treated with adefovir dipivoxil (ADV) since 2005.

Whole-body bone scintigraphy showed multiple lesions with increased uptake, indicating insidious pathological fractures caused by hypophosphatemic osteomalacia.
